Session `ygm/20260804_221748` annotated YGM (LLNL header-only C++ MPI messaging library) and its companion benchmark ygm-bench with dftracer FUNCTION-mode C++ tracing, then scaled up to a validated 4-node/128-rank run on Tuolumne.

Key thread: the first dftracer install (a prebuilt prerelease wheel) had no MPI support compiled in, so it was replaced with a from-source build matched to YGM's own `PrgEnv-gnu` toolchain (avoiding a double-MPI-runtime link risk). Annotation hit a header-only include-order pitfall (fixed by adding the dftracer include to every header, not just the entry .cpp) and, at scale, a hot-loop over-annotation problem where 9 progress-poll functions made traced runs 5-10x slower — fixed via dftracer's own selective aggregation feature rather than stripping instrumentation. Separately, scaling ygm-bench's `around_the_world_ygm` benchmark surfaced two real system findings: an OOM at high rank density from default receive-buffer sizing, and a ~400x collapse in `MPI_Iallreduce` throughput as rank density increased on Cray MPICH — settled on 32 ranks/node as the working configuration. The final validated run (128 ranks, 11.0 minutes, 716,800 hops) confirmed the Iallreduce collapse as the genuine bottleneck at scale, not a tracing artifact.

This report-assembly pass verified the above against the actual workspace filesystem, wrote the one missing reproduction script (`run_scaled_ygm_bench.sh`, since the final run was launched ad hoc via `flux submit`/`flux jobs` with no saved wrapper), reconciled a duplicate skill (`workload-ygm` merged into the correctly-named `software-ygm`), and assembled this `final_report/` package.
